release: Discover Library Index & Cache Write Coalescing
name: Discover Library Index & Cache Write Coalescing
changes: Builds one signature-aware Discover library lookup index per media-library.json generation so card decoration no longer reparses and linearly scans the multi-megabyte Automation library for every title.
Updates metadata-cache.json in memory immediately but coalesces bursty cache puts into one short-delay compact atomic disk flush instead of rewriting the entire cache once per metadata response.
Uses a cross-process metadata-cache flush lock and signature reload so desktop/service peer changes are merged before a coalesced write while dirty local responses remain available in memory.
Extends Discover diagnostics with library-index build/hit timing and metadata-cache write-request/coalescing/dirty/flush telemetry.
Uses interpolated Discover percentiles and adds average/sample counts so tiny diagnostic samples are not misrepresented.
Preserves v3.6.59 stale-while-revalidate detail, prefetch/view separation, Metadata Server v0.3.3, v3.6.58 Automation reconciliation, and private SABnzbd 5.1.2.
regression_guards: Repeated Discover library-status lookups parse/build the library index once, then reuse it until the media-library.json signature changes; direct metadata/TMDB/title matching keeps the previous semantics.
Multiple metadata cache puts remain immediately readable from memory and persist through one explicit coalesced flush, with peer-process records merged before the write.
Metadata cache write telemetry distinguishes write requests from actual disk writes and exposes coalesced requests, dirty keys, deferrals and failures.
Two-sample Discover p50 uses the interpolated midpoint and route telemetry exposes average/sample counts.
All v3.6.59 and earlier regression guards remain mandatory; SAB transfer/repair/extraction architecture and terminal-history schema remain unchanged.
